bullets.text: Cloud computing is the delivery of computing services over the internet.
It includes servers, storage, databases, networking, software, and AI.
Users rent computing resources instead of buying and maintaining them.
Analogy: paying for electricity without owning the power plant.
Makes technology more affordable, scalable, and convenient.
On-demand self-service: access resources without human interaction.
Broad network access: available over the internet from various devices.
Resource pooling: providers share resources across multiple customers.
Rapid elasticity: resources scale up or down quickly based on demand.
Measured service: usage is monitored and billed based on consumption.
Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS): delivers fundamental computing resources like VMs and storage (e.g., AWS EC2).
Platform as a Service (PaaS): provides infrastructure plus a development platform (e.g., Google App Engine).
Software as a Service (SaaS): delivers ready-to-use applications over the internet (e.g., Gmail, Microsoft 365, Zoom).
Public cloud: services shared by multiple organizations over the internet.
Private cloud: dedicated to a single organization for more control and security.
Hybrid cloud: combines public and private clouds for flexibility and security.
Community cloud: shared by organizations with common goals or requirements.
Reduced costs: no heavy investment in hardware or maintenance.
Improved scalability: easily expand or reduce resources as needed.
Enhanced flexibility: access applications and data from anywhere.
Reliability: providers offer backup, disaster recovery, and high availability.
Supports innovation: faster deployment and experimentation.
Security and privacy: trusting providers to protect sensitive data.
Downtime: outages can affect access to critical resources.
Compliance: adhering to strict regulations for data storage.
Vendor lock-in: difficulty and cost in switching providers.
Performance concerns: for applications requiring high speed or low latency.
Data storage and backup (Google Drive, Dropbox).
Business collaboration (Slack, Microsoft Teams) and entertainment (Netflix, Spotify).
Healthcare, education, and research utilize cloud solutions.
Cloud computing powers AI and big data analytics by providing high-performance resources.
Edge computing processes data closer to the source, relying on the cloud for storage and management.
Multi-cloud strategies for avoiding vendor lock-in and improving reliability.
Serverless computing allows developers to focus on code, not infrastructure.
Continued focus on security, compliance, and advanced technologies.
Integration with AI, blockchain, and 5G will expand possibilities.
Cloud computing offers flexibility, scalability, and cost savings, shaping our digital world.
